author: Mir Amman
first_published: 1804, Calcutta (Hindoostanee Press, for the College of Fort William); written 1801–1802 (1215–1217 AH)
edition: The Bagh o Bahar for the Examination of Military Officers and Others by the Higher and Lower Standards, published by authority under the editorship of Major D. C. Phillott, Secretary, Board of Examiners, Calcutta. Fourth edition, Calcutta: Baptist Mission Press, 1905 (title page, scan page 3; the archive.org record gives the year as 1860, which is wrong). 379 pages of Urdu text. Scan: Digital Library of India copy from the Maulana Azad Library, Aligarh Muslim University. Only Mir Amman's text is used.
description: Mir Amman's tale of the four dervishes and King Azad Bakht, written in plain Delhi Urdu at Fort William College in 1801–1802 and counted as the first classic of modern Urdu prose.
translation_note: Faithful English translation made for this library, paragraph by paragraph. Verse is rendered couplet by couplet, accuracy before rhyme. Each reading section covers about four pages of the 1905 edition.
transcription_note: The digital base text is the Urdu Wikisource transcription (ur.wikisource.org/wiki/باغ_و_بہار), proofread section by section against the page images of the 1905 Phillott edition; dropped words and misreadings were corrected to the scan. Spelling follows modern Urdu usage. Mir Amman's petition to the College (section 1) and the closing verses with the chronogram (last section) are not printed in the 1905 edition and are given from the Wikisource text of the first edition; the order of the closing couplets was restored from the rhyme. Gilchrist's English preface and the editor's matter are not included.
